purpose: Per CEO R296 P0+P1: 'Do not assume public dataset. Create explicit dataset-state machine. Start with MAUDE. Model limitations. Attack P-13 before building — collision check against existing AI implant failure prediction.'
constitutional_basis: Article XXV (unknown must remain unknown — dataset suitability is NOT assumed). Article XXXII (state strongest alternative explanation — existing AI failure prediction is the alternative).

P0_dataset_state_machine.transition_rule: Each transition requires explicit verification. If any stage fails, P-13 EV automatically recalculates. No state is skipped.
P0_dataset_state_machine.anti_assumption_rule: The machine must NOT assume a dataset exists until FOUND is verified. The machine must NOT assume a dataset is usable until SUITABLE is verified.

dataset_candidates_assessed.name: MIMIC-IV
dataset_candidates_assessed.access: CREDENTIALED — requires CITI training + data use agreement + PhysioNet credentialing
dataset_candidates_assessed.is_public: NO — credentialed access, not immediately downloadable
dataset_candidates_assessed.implant_failure_data: MIMIC-IV is clinical ICU data. May contain some device-related adverse events but NOT specifically structured for implant failure prediction.
dataset_candidates_assessed.limitation: Access takes 1-4 weeks for credentialing. Not a $0 immediate dataset.
dataset_candidates_assessed.verdict: ACCESS_NOT_IMMEDIATELY_AVAILABLE — requires credentialing process. Not suitable as first test.

dataset_candidates_assessed.name: FDA MAUDE (Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience)
dataset_candidates_assessed.access: PUBLIC — downloadable MDR files + openFDA API
dataset_candidates_assessed.implant_failure_data: Tens of millions of records. Contains device adverse event reports including implant failures, malfunctions, and patient deaths.
dataset_candidates_assessed.limitation: FDA EXPLICITLY WARNS: MAUDE is passive surveillance. Reports are incomplete, inaccurate, unverified, and biased. Incidence/prevalence CANNOT be inferred from MAUDE alone. MAUDE = adverse-event signal discovery, NOT clinical-performance ground truth.
dataset_candidates_assessed.what_maude_CAN_support: Failure-mode discovery/classification. Identifying common failure modes. Training a classifier to categorize failure types.
dataset_candidates_assessed.what_maude_CANNOT_support: Predictive failure rate. Clinical performance validation. Incidence estimation. Prospective prediction accuracy.
dataset_candidates_assessed.tooling: Stanford/AutonLab fda_maude GitHub repo provides download/wrangling scripts: https://github.com/autonlab/fda_maude
dataset_candidates_assessed.verdict: SUITABLE for failure-mode classification. NOT SUITABLE for predictive accuracy validation. Must be paired with clinical data for prediction validation.
dataset_candidates_assessed.state_after_assessment: FOUND + ACCESS_VERIFIED + LICENSE_VERIFIED (public domain). Labels and sample size need verification.

dataset_candidates_assessed.name: Hydrocephalus Clinical Research Network (HCRN)
dataset_candidates_assessed.access: RESTRICTED — research network data, requires IRB + DUA
dataset_candidates_assessed.implant_failure_data: HCRN has published shunt failure data (33,248 pediatric patients in 2023 ML study). But the dataset itself is not publicly downloadable.
dataset_candidates_assessed.limitation: Published studies used HCRN data, but raw data requires research collaboration agreement.

dataset_candidates_assessed.name: NSQIP (National Surgical Quality Improvement Program)
dataset_candidates_assessed.access: RESTRICTED — ACS NSQIP requires hospital participation + data use agreement
dataset_candidates_assessed.implant_failure_data: Surgical outcomes data including some implant-related complications. But not specifically structured for implant failure prediction.

P0_dataset_assessment_result.best_immediate_option: MAUDE — public, downloadable, has tooling (AutonLab scripts)
P0_dataset_assessment_result.maude_limitation_must_flow_into_evidence: MAUDE = adverse-event signal discovery, NOT incidence or clinical-performance ground truth. Any model trained on MAUDE can classify failure MODES but cannot predict failure RATES or prospective accuracy.
P0_dataset_assessment_result.what_this_means_for_P13: P-13 can use MAUDE to build a failure-mode CLASSIFIER (which types of failures occur). But P-13 CANNOT use MAUDE alone to prove predictive accuracy (how well does the model predict future failures?). Predictive validation requires clinical data (HCRN, MIMIC-IV, or prospective study).
P0_dataset_assessment_result.revised_P13_evidence_path: Step 1: MAUDE failure-mode classifier (adverse event classification). Step 2: If classifier shows interesting patterns, approach buyer with MAUDE evidence. Step 3: Buyer provides clinical data for predictive validation. Step 4: Neuromorphic model comparison.
P0_dataset_assessment_result.p13_ev_impact: P-13 EV is REDUCED from $36K to ~$20K. The quick-win thesis is WEAKER than assumed. MAUDE can support a first evidence step ($0) but not a full validation. The optimizer should re-rank.
P0_dataset_assessment_result.honest_label: P-13 is no longer a $0 quick win. It is a $0 first step (MAUDE classification) that requires additional clinical data for full validation. The portfolio optimizer must reflect this.

P1_collision_attack_on_P13.question: What does neuromorphic/on-device prediction technically accomplish that conventional ML cannot?

existing_art_identified.description: Hip prosthesis failure prediction through radiological deep sequence learning. Multicenter Hip-Net study, 1,454 patients / 2,908 radiographs. Classifies 5 hip-failure causes. External validation performed.
existing_art_identified.implication: AI implant failure prediction with external validation ALREADY EXISTS for orthopedic implants. P-13's 'AI predicts failure' claim is NOT novel for this domain.

existing_art_identified.description: ML models for shunt complications in 33,248 pediatric patients. ROC AUC 0.733. Independently validated.
existing_art_identified.implication: AI shunt failure prediction with independent validation ALREADY EXISTS. P-13's 'AI predicts shunt failure' claim is NOT novel.

existing_art_identified.description: Hydrocephalus system with controller, sensors, obstruction detection, AI/ML possibilities.
existing_art_identified.implication: The patent landscape already contemplates AI/ML in shunt systems.

P1_collision_attack_on_P13.collision_verdict: P-13's 'AI predicts implant failure' is NOT a differentiator. The field is crowded. P-13 MUST find a different value proposition.

potential_differentiators_to_test.test: Is on-device prediction materially better than cloud prediction for any clinical scenario?
potential_differentiators_to_test.moat_strength: WEAK — most implant monitoring already uses cloud. On-device is a feature, not a moat.

potential_differentiators_to_test.test: Does neuromorphic computing enable prediction at <1mW where conventional ML cannot?
potential_differentiators_to_test.moat_strength: MODERATE — if the power budget is truly constraining, neuromorphic may be the only option. But most implantable devices have enough power for periodic cloud upload.

potential_differentiators_to_test.test: Does continuous event-driven sensing detect failure earlier than periodic cloud upload?
potential_differentiators_to_test.moat_strength: MODERATE — if the failure develops over minutes (not hours/days), continuous monitoring matters. But most implant failures develop over days-weeks.

potential_differentiators_to_test.test: Is there a clinical or regulatory scenario where data cannot leave the device?
potential_differentiators_to_test.moat_strength: WEAK — HIPAA-compliant cloud upload is standard practice.

potential_differentiators_to_test.test: Is there a clinical scenario where the patient has no connectivity for extended periods?
potential_differentiators_to_test.moat_strength: WEAK — most patients in developed markets have connectivity.

P1_collision_attack_on_P13.collision_attack_result: P-13's strongest potential differentiator is 'ultra-low-power on-device prediction enabling chronic implantation without battery replacement.' But this is CONDITIONAL on: (a) the power budget being truly constraining (needs P-08/P-15 energy budget analysis), (b) conventional ML being too power-hungry for chronic implantation (needs benchmarking), (c) the prediction being clinically useful when generated on-device (needs clinical evidence).
P1_collision_attack_on_P13.p13_revised_positioning: P-13 is NOT 'AI predicts implant failure.' P-13 is POTENTIALLY 'ultra-low-power on-device failure prediction enabling chronic implantable monitoring without battery replacement.' The neuromorphic computing is the POTENTIAL differentiator, not the prediction itself.
P1_collision_attack_on_P13.p13_ev_after_collision: P-13 EV FURTHER REDUCED. The prediction is not novel. The neuromorphic differentiator is conditional on power budget analysis (P-08/P-15). P-13 should be DEPRIORITIZED until P-08/P-15 energy budgets confirm that conventional ML is too power-hungry for chronic implantation.
P1_collision_attack_on_P13.p13_new_state: COMMERCIAL_FRAMED (downgraded from quick-win candidate to conditional candidate)
P1_collision_attack_on_P13.p13_new_rank: DROPS from #1 to ~#8. The $0 dataset quick-win thesis is REFUTED. MAUDE can support a first step but not a quick transaction. P-13 is now a CONDITIONAL candidate that depends on P-08/P-15 results.

layer_1_modelled_EV.description: Our internal estimate. No external evidence.
layer_1_modelled_EV.rule: Can be used for INTERNAL portfolio ranking. CANNOT be used in buyer-facing materials. CANNOT be stated as 'expected value' to buyers.

layer_2_calibrated_EV.description: Updated by computational/experimental evidence (but NOT by buyer behavior).
layer_2_calibrated_EV.formula: P_technical(CALIBRATED) × P_buyer(MODELLED or CALIBRATED) × value(TIER_1 or TIER_2) − cost
layer_2_calibrated_EV.rule: Can be used in buyer-facing materials WITH explicit 'MODELLED EV based on computational evidence' label. P_buyer must still be MODELLED unless buyer has responded.

layer_3_buyer_verified_EV.description: Updated ONLY from actual buyer behavior.
layer_3_buyer_verified_EV.formula: P_technical(CALIBRATED or BUYER_VERIFIED) × P_buyer(BUYER_VERIFIED) × value(TIER_3 or higher) − cost
layer_3_buyer_verified_EV.rule: CAN be used in buyer-facing materials as 'buyer-verified value.' Requires: buyer has explicitly stated WTP (Tier 3) or made offer (Tier 4) or paid (Tier 5).

P2_three_layer_EV_upgrade.machine_enforcement_rule: The optimizer MUST reject any claim that uses Tier 1 modelled WTP as if it were Tier 3 buyer WTP. If WTP_state != BUYER_VERIFIED, the machine labels the EV as MODELLED and prevents buyer-confidence claims. This is a HARD CONSTRAINT, not a recommendation.

track_A_quick_commercial_evidence.principle: Cheapest evidence first. Each candidate must pass its cheapest evidence gate before advancing. P-13 has been DEPRIORITIZED — its $0 dataset quick-win thesis was refuted by MAUDE limitations + collision attack.
track_A_quick_commercial_evidence.next_24_hours: P-15 and P-08 energy budget computations ($0-5K each, purely computational, no external data needed).

track_B_flagship.principle: Highest absolute value. Physical bench + Miethke evaluation.
track_B_flagship.next_24_hours: Send Buyer Evaluation Kit to Miethke.

track_C_scientific_development.next_24_hours: P-04: engage enzyme collaborator. P-09: engage medicinal chemistry consultant.

transitions.OUTREACH_SENT → RESPONSE: Buyer replies (any response — positive, negative, or question)
transitions.RESPONSE → TECHNICAL_INTEREST: Buyer asks technical question or requests more detail
transitions.TECHNICAL_INTEREST → EVALUATION_COMMITME: Buyer says 'send us the package; we'll evaluate it'
transitions.EVALUATION_COMMITMENT → DATA_REQUEST: Buyer asks for specific data, test results, or clarification
transitions.DATA_REQUEST → TEST: Buyer runs or commissions a test of the technology
transitions.TEST → BUYER_FEEDBACK: Buyer provides feedback (positive, negative, or with objections)
transitions.any_state → REJECTION: Buyer explicitly rejects at any stage. Rejection is NOT failure — it is portfolio evidence. Rejection reason enters BUYER_FEEDBACK_INTAKE_SCHEMA and may create new requirement/test.

P5_buyer_loop_state_machine.provenance_required_for_every_state: Each state transition requires: timestamp, buyer_id, evidence_type (email/letter/PO), evidence_hash, operator (who recorded it).
P5_buyer_loop_state_machine.rejection_is_evidence: A buyer rejection at any stage is recorded as portfolio evidence. The rejection reason (technology/economics/integration/timing/evidence) updates P_buyer from MODELLED to CALIBRATED. This IMPROVES the optimizer's accuracy even though the individual candidate didn't transact.

P4_P11_evidence_program.question: Can a specific phage + immobilization architecture survive long enough and retain enough activity to prevent biofilm on an orthopedic implant surface?
evidence_chain: phage_selection → target_organism (S. aureus, S. epidermidis) → surface_material (titanium, PEEK, cobalt-chrome) → immobilization_mechanism (covalent, entrapment, adsorption) → retained_activity (phage titer after immobilization) → biofilm_reduction (in vitro assay) → cytocompatibility (mammalian cell viability) → manufacturing_feasibility (can it be produced at scale?) → buyer_integration (which implant product?)
P4_P11_evidence_program.smallest_experiment: Literature review: identify 3-5 phage species effective against S. aureus biofilm. Identify 2-3 immobilization chemistries. Assess whether retained activity after immobilization has been demonstrated in any published work. Cost: $5-15K, 2-4 weeks.
P4_P11_evidence_program.go_no_go_gate: If NO published evidence of phage survival after immobilization on implant surfaces → P-11 is HIGH RISK. If published evidence exists → P-11 advances to in vitro design.
